samples.summary: `skipped` is derived from job conclusions, but ci.yml's heavy jobs are never skipped as jobs — so a reduced run is always reported as "Full CI / No job was skipped"
samples.evidence: ci-report.yml:164-174 computes `skipped` as `HEAVY.filter(j => j.conclusion === 'skipped')`. But ci.yml deliberately does NOT gate `verify-browser`/`verify-integration` at job level (ci.yml:293-324, 405-426: "THE FILTER IS ON THE STEPS, NOT ON THIS JOB"); each step carries `if: env.RUN_HEAVY == 'true'` and the job "reports success in seconds" (ci.yml:317, 361, 483). A job whose steps were all skipped has conclusion `success`, not `skipped`. Therefore `skipped` is `[]` on every reduced run, the write step falls into the final `else` branch (ci-report.yml:340-342) and posts "### Full CI / No job was skipped", and the `areas.reasons` plus the `full-ci` hint (lines 335-339) are unreachable in practice. The comment's entire stated payload — "what CI skipped" — is inverted for exactly the case it exists for, and this is a regression: the removed code derived the "Reduced run" banner from `areas.full === false`, which was correct.

samples.summary: The one case where the heavy jobs really do have conclusion `skipped` is a verify-self FAILURE, which is then mislabelled "Reduced CI" with advice to add the `full-ci` label
samples.evidence: ci.yml:324 / 426 gate both heavy jobs with `if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.verify-self.result == 'success' }}`, so their only route to `conclusion === 'skipped'` is verify-self failing (or the job being genuinely skipped upstream). ci-report.yml:335-339 renders that as `### Reduced CI` / `Skipped: verify-browser, verify-integration` / "Add the **`full-ci`** label and re-run to force the whole suite." On a red PR the reviewer is told the scope was reduced and offered a label that cannot help, with no mention that CI failed. The scope signal and the failure signal are conflated, in the direction that hides the failure.

samples.summary: The `gatingFiles` branch is checked first and unconditionally claims the whole suite ran, even when the run was reduced or its scope unknown
samples.evidence: The label decision (ci-report.yml:220-251) matches PR files against `ci.ciConfig` read from the DEFAULT BRANCH, while ci.yml's actual scope came from `scripts/changed-areas.mjs` running against the PR's own `harness.config.json` (classify() at changed-areas.mjs:402-412). When the two disagree — a PR that edits `harness.config.json` to drop a glob, or any drift between head and base config — `gating_files` is non-empty while the run was reduced, and because `if (gatingFiles && gatingFiles.length > 0)` (line 322) is the FIRST branch it prints "### Full CI — a gating file changed … this one is measured by the whole suite" and suppresses both the `skipped` report and the `skipped === null` "scope unknown" fallback (lines 329-343). That is precisely the "quietly-wrong reporting" the removed comment at old line ~215 warned about, reintroduced through branch ordering.

samples.summary: An unhandled throw in the resolve step now suppresses the comment entirely and fails the workflow, where the old single step at least attempted a report
samples.evidence: `Resolve what to report` (line 97) has no `continue-on-error`, and `github.rest.repos.listPullRequestsAssociatedWithCommit` (line 122) plus `github.rest.pulls.get`'s surrounding code paths are outside any try/catch (only the jobs listing, getContent and listFiles are wrapped). Any transient API failure there throws, the step fails, `steps.resolve.outputs.pr_number` is empty, so `if: steps.resolve.outputs.pr_number != ''` (line 269) skips the write step and no comment is posted — while the job itself goes red on main, which is the failure mode the new tests' own preamble says nobody notices. Wrapping the resolution in a try/catch (or making the step's failure non-fatal) would keep the report's "could not determine" path reachable.

samples.summary: The new guard tests assert only token plumbing, so neither would have caught the skipped-job logic error above; the `readers`/`writers` sets are hardcoded and silently vacuous if an endpoint is renamed
samples.evidence: `READS`/`WRITES` (ci-workflow.test.mjs:312-322) are literal substrings. `readers.length > 0` and `writers.length > 0` (328-329) only prove that at least one listed string appears somewhere; a future read added on the App token via an endpoint not in the list (e.g. `issues.listLabelsOnIssue`, `repos.getBranch`) passes unnoticed, and the test comment at 306-310 asserts "the split is therefore only ever enforced by this test" — which is true, and is why the enumeration being non-exhaustive is a correctness gap in the guard itself rather than a style point.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. ci-report.yml:170-174 derives `skipped` from `j.conclusion === 'skipped'` for `verify-browser`/`verify-integration`, but ci.yml deliberately never skips those jobs at job level: their `if:` is `!cancelled() && needs.verify-self.result == 'success'` (ci.yml:324, ci.yml:426) and the path filter lives on each step via `if: env.RUN_HEAVY == 'true'` (ci.yml:358-396, 480-499), with a "Why this job is doing nothing" step so the job runs and reports success in seconds (ci.yml:357-361, 479-483). scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:67-108 enforces this invariant by banning `outputs.heavy`/`outputs.full`/`full-ci` in any matrix job's job-level `if:`. Therefore on every reduced run `skipped` is `[]`, not `null`, so the write step skips the `skipped === null` branch (ci-report.yml:329) and the `skipped.length > 0` branch (ci-report.yml:335) and lands on ci-report.yml:340-342, posting "### Full CI / No job was skipped" for exactly the reduced runs the comment exists to report. The `areas.reasons` list and the `full-ci` hint (ci-report.yml:338-339) are unreachable on that path, and the only case that does produce a `skipped` conclusion is a `verify-self` failure — i.e. the branch fires when scope was not reduced. This is inverted logic producing wrong reported state, in the correctness lane; no guard elsewhere prevents it.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. ci-report.yml:322 makes gatingFiles the first branch, printing "### Full CI — a gating file changed … this one is measured by the whole suite" and making both the skipped===null "scope unknown" branch (329-334) and the "Reduced CI" branch (335-339) unreachable. gatingFiles is computed from ci.ciConfig read off the DEFAULT branch (ci-report.yml:220-226) matched against pulls.listFiles (238-251), while the run's real scope came from changed-areas.mjs executed on the PR-head checkout (ci.yml:90-105) using the head's own config in classify() (changed-areas.mjs:400-415) — structurally different inputs that can disagree. Two divergence paths are reachable without any config edit: (1) verify-browser/verify-integration are job-level skipped when verify-self fails (ci.yml:324, ci.yml:426), so skipped is non-empty, yet any PR touching .github/workflows/** (a ciConfig glob, harness.config.json:52-62) takes the first branch and suppresses the skip report; (2) a failed listJobsForWorkflowRun (ci-report.yml:175-177) leaves skipped null and the deliberate "scope unknown" fallback is overridden. classify()'s unmapped-path fallback (changed-areas.mjs:435-448) narrows but does not close the head/base config-drift case. No guard or test constrains the branch ordering — a grep for gating_files/Reduced CI matched only this workflow file. Impact is confined to comment content rather than a crash, but reporting the scope decision is this comment's stated sole purpose (ci-report.yml:288-292), so the ordering bug is real and in-lane.
